Subject: Re: Bulk vendor CSV for onboarding (120 rows)

Hi Claire — thanks for sending this over. We kicked off an automatic ingest but ran into validation errors on a subset of rows. Quick summary of the most common issues: 

- company_name contains diacritics and non-ASCII punctuation that our normalizer split into separate entities
- multiple rows missing or malformed tax_id (EIN/VAT) causing dedupe to fail
- contact_email column has a handful of alias-only addresses (e.g., procurement@domain without suffix)
- whitespace/prefix characters in the registration number field

I've attached a short report with sample failed rows and the specific validation messages (invite_report-20260822.csv). We'll hold on sending invites until we have a cleaned file so we don't create duplicate supplier records.

CC'ing Ben — he owns our bulk onboarding scripts and can run a normalization pass if you want us to. If you'd prefer to make edits on your side, please ensure the CSV includes these canonical headers: company_name, tax_id, contact_email, phone, country, address_line1.

Next steps:
- Ben to run normalization/dedupe and return a cleaned CSV for your review (if you approve, we'll retry invites)
- We will not send live invites until Claire signs off to avoid duplicate supplier records

Best,
Camila Reyes
Onboarding Specialist | Redwood Inference
attachments: invite_report-20260822.csv (CSV, 4KB)

On Sun, Aug 22, 2026 at 10:04 AM Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Claire — thanks for sending this over. We kicked off an automatic ingest but ran into validation errors on a subset of rows. Quick summary of the most common issues: 
> - company_name contains diacritics and non-ASCII punctuation that our normalizer split into separate entities
> - multiple rows missing or malformed tax_id (EIN/VAT) causing dedupe to fail

Thanks Camila — I ran our cleanup and dedupe routine against the file. Summary of actions: 

- Normalized names (strip diacritics, unify punctuation), trimmed stray control characters
- Applied tax_id pattern validation and flagged rows where the id didn't match a country schema
- Canonicalized emails (lowercase, added domain fallback for known corporate aliases)
- Merged likely duplicates based on tax_id + address similarity; left explicit duplicates as separate when tax_id missing

I've attached the cleaned CSV (bulk_invite_cleaned.csv, 13KB) and a quick mapping log. The rows that remain flagged need confirmation of correct tax_id — I added a "needs_review" column.

If Silverpine confirms that we should always merge by tax_id, I can re-run the merge to collapse the remaining entries. Otherwise we'll proceed to create distinct supplier records for rows without a validated tax_id.

Attachments: bulk_invite_cleaned.csv (CSV, 13KB)

Let me know if you'd like us to proceed with the invite run. If you approve, we'll trigger invites in a controlled batch (25 invites at a time) and return an invite_report CSV with result codes (sent/bounced/already_active).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Manager, Onboarding Automation | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben and Camila — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick confirmations: 

- Please proceed with invites for the 120 rows in the cleaned file.
- Merge policy: yes, prefer merge by tax_id where present. For rows without tax_id, do not force-merge — create distinct supplier entries and mark them for follow-up.
- Please deliver the invite report when the run completes (bounced/accepted/active). We will prioritize follow-up for the "needs_review" rows next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If possible, can you also share the dedupe heuristic notes you used so our data team can mirror them in our ERP export?

Claire
